author: TEDx Talks
description:
What does it really take to prepare humans for life beyond Earth? In this talk, we are taken inside one of the world’s largest Mars simulation missions, where isolation, limited resources, and extreme conditions reveal not only technical challenges, but deeply human ones.

Through personal experience, the talk explores who gets to be part of humanity’s next giant leap, and why diversity, identity, and belonging may be just as critical to space exploration as rockets and technology. Mackenzie Calle is an American artist whose project The Gay Space Agency reimagines the history of space exploration through a queer lens. Combining archival NASA imagery and original photography, she highlights the untold stories of LGBTQ+ pioneers and imagines a more inclusive cosmic future. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: I lived in a Mars simulation—here’s what I learned | Mackenzie Calle | TEDxTallinn

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the economy isn’t driven by numbers first, but by people?

In this TEDxUniversiteitvanAmsterdam talk, Aarya Sharma explores the deeply human side of economics. From a €15 gift card that brought three days of relief, to the invisible calculations behind everyday choices, she reflects on how studying economics can rewire the way we live: comparing costs, weighing trade-offs, and chasing rational decisions in an irrational world.

But history tells a more complicated story. From Tulip Mania in 17th-century Holland to the Dot-com bubble and the 2008 financial crisis, markets have never been shaped by equations alone. They are moved by fear, hope, trust, ambition, desperation, and belief.

Aarya challenges the idea that economics is purely rational. Instead, she invites us to see markets for what they truly are: human systems built by emotional, contradictory, imperfect people. This talk is a reminder that while economics influences how we think and behave, our feelings, perception
title: The emotional side of economics | Aarya Sharma | TEDxUniversiteitVanAmsterdam

description: The North Sea is home to many species of seabirds: auks, loons and gulls, just to name a few. However, we find far more on the bottom of the sea: golden eagles, snowy owls, and extinct penguin-like great auks. These are remnants of the then-dry North Sea of the last ice age: Doggerland. The bottom of the sea floor is deposited onto our beaches, most famously Maasvlakte 2 and the Zandmotor. Here, the fossilised bird bones are picked up by passionate collectors. A remarkable number of these bones belong to ducks, but we did not yet know which ducks. I set out to fill this knowledge gap and analysed 304 fossil duck bones. As it turns out, these ducks were hiding many secrets! What secrets, you may ask? Well, you will simply have to see... Martijn van der Meer (22) actively researches fossil bird remains, primarily from the North Sea. He graduated from Jacob van Liesveldt in 2021 and from his BSc Biology in 2025. author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TEDx talk, Shloka explores the vital distinction between Duty and Service, using the Upanishadic story of Satyakama Jabala to illustrate how a mundane task can become a path to enlightenment. She defines duty as a mandatory "debt" or transaction—an external obligation often performed for paychecks or to avoid penalties . Conversely, service is a voluntary, altruistic offering driven by internal desire and love .
Shloka argues that while duty maintains society, service allows the soul to thrive, releasing a "Helper’s High" of oxytocin and serotonin . She notes that the world faces a "crisis of meaning" because we have perfected systems of duty but neglected the spirit of Seva—selfless service. Ultimately, she challenges the audience to view duty as the "floor" and service as the "ceiling," urging us to find purpose beyond mandates to reach our true greatness as citizens of a shared humanity.

title: Duty Vs Service | Lakshmi Sloka Durgam | TEDxParamita High School

description:
Aadya, a 10th-grade student at Paramita High School, delivers a compelling TEDx talk challenging the global obsession with academic grades. Using Srinivasa Ramanujan’s story as a foundation, she argues that grades are merely "snapshots" of memory and compliance rather than true measures of intelligence.
The talk highlights that while the current grading system rewards those who follow instructions, it often punishes creativity and problem-solving. Aadya defines true intelligence as a "mosaic" of adaptability, synthesis, and resilience—skills essential for the real world but often ignored on report cards.
She advocates for a transition toward competency-based learning that fosters wisdom over rankings. Integrating Sanskrit proverbs and philosophical quotes, she concludes with the Asato Ma Sadgamaya prayer, emphasizing that education should lead students from the "darkness" of rote memorization toward the "light" of actual potential and divine understanding.

Ultimately, Nimish encourages the audience to discard their scripts, listen to curiosity over fear, and trust that the "profound" and "mysterious" path of life will eventually reveal a magnificent purpose. description:
In a world that rewards being the best, what happens when you choose to be average? Vidhi Adhikari, a sustainability content creator known as "Trashy Sister," shares her journey from being a high-achieving "head girl" to feeling invisible in college, ultimately finding her voice through environmental advocacy. By shifting her focus from competing with others to collaborating for the planet, she explores how the power of individual, imperfect actions can combat the global crisis of waste and climate change.

This talk offers a space to reflect on the parts of ourselves we have dimmed to make the world comfortable and highlights the power found in collective, unapologetic individuality. Vidhi is a creator who navigated the pressures of social media popularity to find one universal truth: you don’t have to be the "best" to be important or to make a difference. title: The Art of Being Average | Vidhi Adhikari | TEDxVivekanandaCollege
